integrity: The proof reduces every capsule placement exactly to a segment placement in the Euclidean inner parallel body of the host. The inner parallel body is compact and convex, the Kakeya property transfers in both directions at the placement level, and Janzer's segment theorem supplies the path. A standalone checker replays the halfspace form of the erosion equivalence and capsule width distinctions; finite checks are explicitly not used as a substitute for the set-theoretic proof.
scientific_limitations: The inheritance argument uses Euclidean-ball thickening, exploiting rotational invariance of the ball. It establishes path-connectivity of the placement space, not the stronger existence of a global continuous orientation selector. The result does not classify all shapes with universal Kakeya rotatability. Differently phrased or unindexed prior observations remain a residual originality risk.
title: Capsules satisfy universal convex Kakeya rotatability
